One point per physical collection · no respawns · symmetric arena · plans apply together. Planning pauses simulated time so serial LLM calls give neither fly a head start.

Black grid: millimetres · green: edible food · grey: solid obstacles · coloured arrows: velocity · bars: energy. Motion is smoothed playback of completed physical steps, slower than real time.

How the body is connected

Virtual chemical/contact sensors drive the 21 sugar inputs. Two downstream pools supply motor drive. Explicit synthetic body reflexes add gradient sampling, exploration, feeding pauses, fatigue and contact escape; these are adapter rules, not behaviours learned by the fly connectome. Zero neural drive cannot propel a resting body. No LLM is involved.

Plans and measured results

Plans and forecasts are generated statements. Food scores, distance, collisions and latency are measured. The same local model plays both flies with separate contexts. Download the control log for exact prompts/actions. One match is an exploratory comparison, not proof of general reasoning ability.

SENSORY / NEURAL / MOTOR

Physical neural control

NO LLM

Two intact FlyWire networks run in lockstep with the world. Each neural step receives current sensory input before the body moves.

Continuous mode builds one network and carries its neuron state, delayed signals and random sequence forward. Activity streams in windows while Llama 2 thinks; the last input stays applied. The target is total downstream spikes per second, across the full network. Llama 2 controls the 21 sugar sensors (25–250 Hz). Simulated time runs slower than wall time on this CPU.

Two-organism mode runs two full networks independently. Llama 2 takes alternating turns to avoid overlapping local inference. The target applies separately to each brain. Both keep running during conversation, so this mode uses more CPU and memory.
